one_liner: Same-day for up to 25 customer accounts (with an unverified-app warning); unlimited installs need a reviewed Marketplace listing, which needs 3 active installs first.

start_today.summary: Build the app with the HubSpot CLI, sign the Acceptable Use Policy, and customers can install it through Composio the same day. Until HubSpot reviews and lists it, installs are capped at 25 and users see an unverified-app warning.
limits_before_approval: Marketplace-distribution app: up to 25 installs (developer test accounts don't count) until the listing is approved
Private-distribution OAuth app instead: up to 10 allowlisted accounts (100 if built in a Solutions Partner account)
Unreviewed apps show an unverified-app warning; users must type 'I accept the risk' to connect
Without a verified domain, the install screen also says the app hasn't been verified
HubSpot grants no manual exceptions to the install caps

composio.note: Composio's managed HubSpot app is the fastest start, but Composio's own docs say it is still awaiting HubSpot approval, so users see the 'Connecting an unverified app' warning, and you can only remove optional scopes from it, not add new ones. Your own app gives you your name, your scope set and control over review. It does not remove the warning on day one: your own app shows the unverified-app warning and is capped at 25 installs until HubSpot approves its Marketplace listing. HubSpot triggers in Composio need a public app's App ID and developer API key in any case.

prerequisites.item: A standard HubSpot account (free or paid)
prerequisites.detail: Since August 28, 2025 every standard account has the Development section; separate developer accounts were folded into standard accounts on March 9, 2026.

prerequisites.item: HubSpot CLI (npm) and a personal access key
prerequisites.detail: New apps are built only as CLI projects. Authenticate the CLI with hs account auth using a personal access key. User-level apps need CLI 8.15.0 and platformVersion 2026.09.
Up to 10 free test accounts for test installs; they don't count toward install caps.

prerequisites.item: A domain you control, with DNS access
prerequisites.detail: Used for the verified domain (TXT record) that changes the install warning. One verified domain per account.

prerequisites.item: Composio project and a custom HubSpot auth config
prerequisites.detail: The Composio dashboard shows the redirect URI to put in the app's redirectUrls.

prerequisites.item: For a Marketplace listing: live terms of service, privacy policy, setup guide, support contact and a demo video
prerequisites.detail: Plus at least 3 active installs from unaffiliated production accounts, and acceptance of the Technology Partner Program Agreement.

phases.name: Set up the account and CLI

steps.text: Use (or sign up for) a standard HubSpot account; open Development in the main navigation. Ignore older guides that say to create a separate 'developer account' and click 'Create App': legacy app creation is closed.
Install the HubSpot CLI with npm (npm install -g @hubspot/cli@latest).
Create a personal access key under Development > Keys and run hs account auth to connect the CLI to your account.
Create at least one developer test account under Testing > Test Accounts.

Create a custom HubSpot auth config in Composio and copy the redirect URI the dashboard shows (Composio's docs name https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback; set the same value as oauth_redirect_uri).
Run hs project create and edit app-hsmeta.json: distribution "marketplace", auth.type "oauth", redirectUrls containing the Composio URI (HTTPS required).

Set scopes. Composio suggests keeping requiredScopes minimal (oauth, which HubSpot adds by default) and putting tool scopes in optionalScopes, because each Composio scope must sit in the same category in HubSpot or installs fail.

Decide on access level now: if the app will be listed as an AI connector, it must be user-level (isUserLevel: true on 2026.09) or built on HubSpot's MCP server. An existing account-level app cannot be switched later.
Run hs project upload to deploy the build.
Copy the Client ID and Client secret from the app's Auth page into the Composio auth config, with scopes and optional_scopes matching the HubSpot categories.
Install the app in a developer test account through a Composio connect link and run a few tool calls.

phases.name: Open it to customer accounts (up to 25)

steps.text: On the app's Distribution tab, click Begin publishing and sign the Acceptable Use Policy. Before this, only developer test accounts can install.
Verify your domain under Development > Domain by adding the TXT record HubSpot gives you.
DNS check: usually within an hour, up to 48 hours.
Tell early customers to expect the unverified-app warning (they type 'I accept the risk'), and track installs against the 25 cap; HubSpot advises listing early.
Reach at least 3 active installs: unaffiliated production accounts with successful API activity in the last 30 days.

Draft the listing: integration-specific overview, public setup guide, shared-data table matching every requested scope, pricing that matches your website, support contacts. Check every URL is live and public.
Write the listing demo-video script; record and upload it.
Remove unused scopes; if you need Sensitive Data scopes, request access from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team first.
Agree to the Technology Partner Program Agreement and click Submit for review. Only one app can be in review at a time.
Ecosystem Quality review: initial review within 10 business days; the whole feedback cycle should take no more than 60 days from when feedback is shared.
Reply to reviewer feedback by email and resubmit; HubSpot says resubmissions are prioritized in the queue.
Apply once listed for 6 months with 60+ active installs; submit a demo video. Certification lasts two years and must be renewed.

scopes.purpose: Base OAuth scope; added to every app by default.
Read record owners (users assigned to records).
Read Sensitive Data properties (Enterprise accounts). Marketplace apps must request access from HubSpot first.

approval.trigger: More than 25 customer installs of a marketplace-distribution app (or more than 10 for a private-distribution app). Removing the unverified-app warning entirely also requires HubSpot's review and listing.
reviewers_check: App uses OAuth as its only auth method and a single app ID
At least 3 active installs from unaffiliated production accounts in the last 30 days
Only scopes the app uses, all documented in the Shared data table
Listing content specific to the HubSpot integration, with live setup guide, ToS, privacy policy and support URLs
HubSpot branding and trademark rules (e.g. no 'HubSpot' in your app name)
AI connectors are user-level or built on HubSpot's MCP server
App is on a supported developer platform version and doesn't use classic CRM cards
approval.typical_wait: HubSpot: initial review within 10 business days, and no more than 60 days from when feedback is shared. Developers on the HubSpot community report waits of 2+ weeks.
common_rejections: Listing describes the company instead of the integration
Dead or non-public URLs (HubSpot's crawler checks them)
Shared-data table doesn't match the requested scopes
Requested scopes the app doesn't use
Submitting a second app while one is in review (auto-rejected)

blockers.blocker: Marketplace-distribution apps stop at 25 installs until the listing is approved, and HubSpot grants no exceptions.
blockers.fix: Submit the listing as soon as you have 3 active installs; use the remaining pre-listing installs as the runway.

blockers.blocker: Listing requires 3 active installs from unaffiliated production accounts, so you need real customers before you can scale.
blockers.fix: Onboard design partners within the 25-install window and make sure each makes API calls within 30 days.

blockers.blocker: Users must type 'I accept the risk' to connect an unreviewed app.
blockers.fix: Verify your domain to show who you are, and get listed to remove the warning.

blockers.blocker: An agent product that connects HubSpot to a general-purpose AI assistant counts as an AI connector and can only be listed if it is user-level or built on HubSpot's MCP server; account-level apps can't be converted.
blockers.fix: Decide before building; for a user-level app, set isUserLevel: true on platform 2026.09 from the start. (In November 2025 HubSpot allowed only the read-only MCP route; user-level apps went GA in 2026.09.)

blockers.blocker: User-level apps don't support webhooks, and Composio's HubSpot triggers rely on webhooks from a public app.
blockers.fix: If you need triggers and a user-level listing, plan for polling or a separate account-level app outside the Marketplace.

blockers.blocker: Scope category mismatch between Composio and HubSpot makes installs fail.
blockers.fix: Composio scopes must be Required or Conditionally required in HubSpot; Composio optional_scopes must be Optional in HubSpot. Reconnect accounts after changes.

blockers.blocker: Older setup guides (including Composio's composio.dev/auth/hubspot) describe creating a developer account and a legacy public app in the UI, which is no longer possible.
blockers.fix: Build a projects-based app with the HubSpot CLI.

blockers.blocker: Only one app can be in Marketplace review at a time.
blockers.fix: Queue multiple apps one after another.

blockers.blocker: Composio's managed HubSpot app also shows the unverified-app warning and can't take extra scopes.
blockers.fix: Use your own app for a different scope set or branding; existing connections stay on the managed config until users reconnect.

agent_can: Install the HubSpot CLI and scaffold the project with hs project create
Write app-hsmeta.json: marketplace distribution, OAuth, Composio redirect URI, minimal required scopes
Map each Composio tool to the HubSpot scope it needs and keep categories in sync
Deploy with hs project upload once the CLI is authenticated
Run a test install and tool calls in a developer test account
Draft the listing overview, setup guide, shared-data table and demo-video script
Check that every listing URL is live and public
you_must: Own the HubSpot account and create the personal access key
Copy the client ID and secret into Composio
Sign the Acceptable Use Policy and the Technology Partner Program Agreement
Add the DNS TXT record for domain verification
Find 3 unaffiliated customers who actively use the app
Decide whether the product is an AI connector and pick user-level or account-level
Record the demo video and submit the listing

sources.title: Create a new app using the CLI: prerequisites
sources.quote: To create an app on the latest version of the developer platform, you'll need to install the HubSpot CLI and authenticate it with your account using the `hs account auth` command.

sources.title: HubSpot account types: legacy developer accounts
sources.quote: As of August 28, 2025, all standard HubSpot accounts now have access to the same functionality in the development overview section in the main navigation.

sources.title: HubSpot account types: developer test accounts

sources.title: App listing requirements: installs
sources.quote: Installs: your app must have at least three active, unique installs.

sources.title: App listing requirements: AI connectors
sources.quote: if your app is an AI connector - an app that primarily connects HubSpot to external generative AI tools - it must require user-level permissions by setting access to user-level or be built with HubSpot's MCP Server.

sources.title: App listing requirements: initial review
sources.quote: Once you submit your listing, the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team will complete an initial review within 10 business days.

sources.title: App listing requirements: review duration
sources.quote: The entire app review and feedback process should take no more than 60 days from the time feedback is shared.

sources.title: App listing requirements: OAuth and scopes

sources.title: App listing requirements: one submission at a time
sources.quote: you can only submit one app at a time for approval. Any additional apps submitted while the initial app is being processed will automatically be rejected.

sources.title: Applying for app certification: eligibility
sources.quote: You will not be able to apply unless your app has been listed for at least 6 months and has at least 60 active installs and the needed amount of API traffic.

sources.title: Certification requirements: renewal
sources.quote: App certifications are valid on a rolling basis for two years, and must be renewed.

sources.title: Scopes: oauth

sources.title: Scopes: app scope types

uncertain: Hands-on time and the 3–8 week total are our estimates; the total depends mostly on how fast you get 3 active, unaffiliated installs.
Real listing waits are community-reported only (one developer: 'more than 2 weeks', May 2026); HubSpot publishes 10 business days for the first review and 60 days from feedback as an upper bound.

Whether an agent product built on Composio counts as an 'AI connector' (an app that 'primarily connects HubSpot to external generative AI tools') is HubSpot's call; a vertical agent may or may not fall under it.
Whether Composio's HubSpot toolkit works with a user-level app is not documented by Composio; user-level apps support only part of the REST API and no webhooks.

Whether users still have to type 'I accept the risk' once your domain is verified (but the app is not yet listed) is not stated clearly; HubSpot says a verified-domain app still shows a banner that it hasn't been reviewed.
The 'resubmissions are prioritized' step comes from a HubSpot staff reply on the community forum, not from the docs, so it is marked uncertain.
No steps are marked tested: HubSpot's authorize page validates in the browser, so our no-account probes only confirmed the token endpoints are live.
